title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from previous pages). k is a commutative ring. S = k{T} = Γ_k(T) is the divided-power polynomial algebra, with T^{(i)}T^{(j)} = c_{ij}T^{(i+j)} and c_{ij} = binom(i+j,i). For a k-module M and N ≥ 0, the 'shadow' (ombre) of order N is the graded S-module ω_N(M) = ⊕_{i≥N} M·T^{(i)}, a submodule of ω_0(M) = M⊗_k S.

The 'théorème' used here. If a family (ξ_i)_{i≥N} in a k-module satisfies c_{ij}(ξ_{i+j} − ξ_i) = 0 for all i ≥ N and j ≥ 1, then the ξ_i are all equal.

Corollaire 1. (a) ω_N is fully faithful. (b) M ≅ {(x_i) ∈ ∏_{i≥N} M T^{(i)} : T^{(j)}x_i = c_{ij}x_{i+j}}.

Proof of (a) on this page:
- A graded S-linear map ω_N(M) → ω_N(M') is a family of k-linear maps u_i : M → M' (i ≥ N).
- Compatibility with multiplication by T^{(j)} is the commutative square shown. Concretely it says c_{ij}(u_{i+j} − u_i) = 0 for all i ≥ N, j ≥ 1, applied pointwise to elements.
- By the theorem all u_i are equal, so Hom_k(M,M') ≅ Hom_{gr S-mod}(ω_N M, ω_N M').

Remark 1. ω_N has a right adjoint π_N, with π_N(𝓜) = {(x_i)_{i≥N} ∈ ∏ 𝓜_i : x_i T^{(j)} = c_{ij}x_{i+j}}. Condition (b) says exactly that the unit M → π_Nω_N(M) is an isomorphism. Hence (a) ⇔ (b), by the standard fact that a left adjoint is fully faithful iff its unit is an isomorphism.

Remark 2. ω_N(M) = S^{+(N)}·ω_0(M) = τ_{≥N}(ω_{N'}(M)) for N ≥ N' ≥ 0 (truncation). The next page draws two conclusions from this:
- The ω_N get coarser as N grows but all stay fully faithful.
- One should pass to the category Omb(k) of graded S-modules ('virtual shadows'), localized by N-negligible and then negligible (S^+-power-torsion) modules. This is a Serre-type quotient, analogous to graded modules modulo torsion for Proj.

Purpose. This builds a 'shadow' formalism, a linear-algebra model of divided-power structures, for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: No error on this page. The required 'théorème' actually holds for every ring k and every N, with no hypothesis needed. Sketch: d = ξ_{i+1} − ξ_i is killed by i+1. For each prime p | i+1, take m large; then binom(p^m−1, i) and binom(p^m−1, i+1) are prime to p (all base-p digits of p^m−1 equal p−1, Lucas). Through ξ_{p^m−1}, this shows d is killed by an integer prime to p. So d = 0 locally at every p dividing i+1, and hence d = 0.
Minor notational slip: the square writes u_i⊗T^{(i)}, and Remark 1 writes x_iT^{(j)} where the previous page has T^{(j)}x_i. Both are harmless because S is commutative.

ideas.what: Shadow functor ω_N(M) = ⊕_{i≥N} M T^{(i)} into graded Γ_k(T)-modules is fully faithful, via the binomial-coefficient lemma
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of pullback/truncation into graded modules over the divided power algebra (QCoh(G_a^♯/G_m))
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; divided-power algebra Γ is classical (Cartan, Roby)

ideas.what: Explicit right adjoint π_N and the equivalence 'fully faithful ⇔ unit iso'
ideas.modern_name: Adjunction unit criterion for full faithfulness

ideas.what: ω_N as truncation τ_{≥N} of M⊗Γ(T), leading (next page) to a category of 'virtual shadows' = graded Γ(T)-modules modulo negligible (S^+-torsion) modules
ideas.modern_name: Serre quotient / Proj-type localization; QCoh of (G_a^♯ minus 0)/G_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (FAC) for graded-modules-mod-torsion; G_a^♯ stacks: Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie (2020s)

missed.claim: Graded k{T}=Γ_k(T)-modules are quasi-coherent sheaves on G_a^♯/G_m, where G_a^♯ = Spec Γ(T) is Drinfeld's PD-hull of the origin. The 'ombre' formalism therefore amounts to studying QCoh(G_a^♯/G_m), and its torsion-quotient to the punctured version. Both are objects central to the modern stacky approach to (prismatic, Hodge–Tate, de Rham) cohomology. In 1976 Grothendieck was building a linear-algebra 'shadow' of PD structures through this very category, aimed at the PD de Rham complex.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor of the G_a^♯/G_m viewpoint (Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie) on divided-power and de Rham phenomena. The surrounding notes may contain further constructions in this language worth comparing to modern stacky approaches.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is routine verification: full faithfulness, an adjoint, truncation. Its interest is that Grothendieck is setting up graded Γ(T)-modules ('ombres virtuelles') and their torsion localization as a framework for the PD de Rham complex. That anticipates G_a^♯/G_m-type ideas, but only implicitly.
transcription_corrections: 'les conditions a) et b) en condition 1' should probably read 'les conditions a) et b) du corollaire 1 sont équivalentes'.
Top arrow of the diagram is labelled T^{(j)} in both rows. The vertical maps are u_i⊗T^{(i)} and u_{i+j}⊗T^{(i+j)}.
